title: Stoichiometry and Reactions - Chemistry - Percent Yield
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What is the formula for Percent Yield?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: A reaction was calculated to produce 50.0 g of product. In the lab, only 45.0 g was recovered. What is the percent yield?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: If the percent yield is 100%, what does this imply?
options: The actual yield is greater than the theoretical yield
The actual yield equals the theoretical yield
questions.explain: 100% yield means the amount obtained experimentally is exactly the amount calculated stoichiometrically.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 20.0 g. If the percent yield is 75.0%, what was the actual yield?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: During an experiment, 12.0 g of product was expected, but 14.0 g was measured. What is the most likely explanation (assuming % yield cannot legitimately exceed 100%)?
options: The product is wet or contains impurities
The limiting reagent was not used up
questions.explain: Yields > 100% usually indicate the product is not dry (contains water) or contains impurities that add mass.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: In the reaction $2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO}$, the theoretical yield of MgO is 8.0 g. If 6.0 g is obtained, what is the percent yield?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Calculate the percent yield if 0.50 moles of reactant A produces 0.40 moles of product B, given the stoichiometry is 1 A : 1 B.
questions.explain: Theoretical is 0.50 moles. Actual is 0.40 moles. $\frac{0.40}{0.50} \times 100 = 80\%$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: If 10.0 g of reactant produces a theoretical yield of 22.0 g of product, but the percent yield is 50%, what is the actual mass of product?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Calculate the percent yield: Reaction of 28.0 g N$_2$ with excess H$_2$ produces 17.0 g NH$_3$. (Theoretical yield calculation required first).
questions.explain: 1 mol N$_2$ (28g) should produce 2 mol NH$_3$ ($2 \times 17.03 = 34.06 \text{ g}$). Theoretical = 34.06 g. Actual = 17.0 g. Yield = $(17.0 / 34.06) \times 100 \approx 50\%$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is the percent yield often less than 100%?
questions.explain: Percent yield is lowered by incomplete reactions, side reactions forming unwanted products, and mechanical loss during transfer or filtration.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: To obtain 50.0 g of product with a reaction known to have a 50% yield, what theoretical yield must you aim for?
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Benzene reacts with Bromine to form Bromobenzene. Theoretical yield = 60 g. Actual yield = 45 g. What is the % yield?
questions.subject: Chemistry
